event: Gilt market crisis after the September mini-budget: LDI pension funds forced to sell, 30-year yields jump over 1 point in days; the Bank of England buys long gilts to restore order.
note: verify: dates and size from memory

event: Fitch downgrades the US from AAA to AA+, citing fiscal deterioration and repeated debt-limit standoffs.
Weak 30-year bond auction: the issue tails by about 5 basis points and dealers take an unusually large share; part of the 2023 term-premium spike.
Moody's cuts China's outlook to negative, citing local-government and state-firm debt.
Fitch cuts China's outlook to negative on rising government debt.
30-year gilt yield reaches its highest since 1998 (about 5.4%); sterling falls at the same time, a sign of fiscal rather than growth worry.
Treasury sell-off after the April tariff announcements: the 10-year yield rises about half a point in a week while the dollar falls.
Moody's downgrades the US from Aaa to Aa1, the last of the three big agencies to drop the top rating.
20-year bond auction tails by about 1 basis point at above 5%; long yields jump the same day.
30-year gilt yield reaches about 5.7%, the highest since 1998, ahead of the autumn Budget.
